items.problem: The agent ran the bare .exe directly (Start-Process ...SimpleImaging.exe) to try to capture output, which produced the misleading REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG event that then poisoned diagnosis.
items.evidence: Session-log turn ~4541 runs the exe directly; the skill explicitly says not to.
items.covered_clearly_at: SKILL.md Step 3 code block: 'winapp build  # compile; never run the .exe directly' and the Diagnosing Startup Crashes section: 'The wrong way to chase it is to sprinkle File.WriteAllText traces ... run this once'.
items.why_no_skill_change: The skill already prominently says never to run the .exe directly and to use Test-AppLaunch. A capable model on re-run should follow it. (The tool's misattribution of the resulting artifact IS a defect and is fixed separately in skill-defects.json item 3 — but the act of running the bare exe is a slip, not a skill gap.)

items.problem: The agent downgraded Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK from 2.2.0 to 1.7.x chasing the crash, which broke deployment (missing-framework 0x80073CF3) and did not fix anything.
items.evidence: Session-log turns ~5585-5720: edits SimpleImaging.csproj to 1.7.260224002 then 1.7.250401001; Test-AppLaunch then reports 'package depends on a framework that could not be found'.
items.covered_clearly_at: plan-and-apply/skill guidance keeps the scaffold's pinned WindowsAppSDK version; SKILL.md Step 2 says reconcile the csproj against the scaffold (which sets the SDK version), not to change the SDK version to chase a runtime crash.
items.why_no_skill_change: Randomly swapping the SDK version is an exploratory misstep, not something the skill invites. With the correct 0xc0000409 guidance in place (added as a defect fix), a re-run would look at the startup XAML instead of the SDK version; no additional 'do not change the SDK version' prose is warranted.
